label: Nico Nico Douga (video upload)
containerCodec: mp4 (recommended; H.264/AVC, H.265/HEVC or AV1 video plus AAC audio), mov (H.264 or H.265 plus AAC or PCM), mkv (H.264 only, plus AAC, PCM or FLAC). AV1 and H.265 are accepted but delivered as H.264 (AVC).
maxSizeNote: 6 GB per file, hard. Doubled from 3 GB on 2024-10-29. The 3 GB figure that older guides and converter sites still repeat is stale, and the 1.5 GB and 100 MB figures that appear in even older guides date from 2016 to 2018. 6 GB is also the practical duration limiter: Nico's own table estimates roughly 60 minutes at 1080p/12 Mbps, about 2 hours at 720p/6 Mbps and about 6 hours at 480p/2 Mbps.
dimensions: Horizontal uploads up to 4096x2160, vertical uploads up to 2160x4096. Frame rate up to 60 fps and it must be a FIXED frame rate (VFR is explicitly rejected). Audio sample rate up to 192 kHz, up to 5.1ch (6ch) accepted but delivered as 2ch. Recommended bitrate: at least 12 Mbps at 1080p, 6 Mbps at 720p, 2 Mbps at 480p. A 1080p rendition is only generated if the upload is at least 1920 px wide or 1080 px high.
note: Page published 2026-04-15, read 2026-09-11, so this is fresh. Limits table verbatim: 'ファイルサイズ | 6GB以下', '解像度 | [横長] 4096x2160以下 [縦長]2160x4096以下', '映像フレームレート | 60fps以下', '音声サンプルレート | 192kHz以下', '音声チャンネル数 | 最大5.1ch（6ch） ※配信時は2chとなります', '動画の長さ | 6時間以下' (file size up to 6 GB; resolution 4096x2160 or 2160x4096; frame rate up to 60 fps; sample rate up to 192 kHz; up to 5.1ch but delivered as 2ch; length up to 6 hours). Recommended format verbatim: 'ファイル形式 | mp4', '映像 | H.264(AVC),High profile 24fps、30fps、60fps の固定フレームレート キーフレーム間隔：10秒以下', '音声 | AAC-LC 48kHz or 96 kHz 192kbps 以上'. Codec support: mp4 = H.264(AVC)/H.265(HEVC)/AV1, mov = H.264/H.265, mkv = H.264, with 'AV1・H.265（HEVC）をご利用の場合：視聴時にはH.264（AVC）に変換されて配信されます'. Re-encode is explicit: '投稿された動画をサーバー側で配信に適した形式へ自動変換しています' (posted videos are automatically converted server-side into a form suited to delivery) and the video is then produced at 1080p/720p/480p/360p/144p. The dedicated encoding guide (qa.nicovideo.jp/faq/show/21908, updated 2026-07-14) adds hard practical requirements: 'MP4 を使用してください。', 'Edit List 機能を用いた編集情報は含めないでください', '映像と音声は同じ長さにしてください', '映像トラックと音声トラックをそれぞれ1つずつ含めてください', '可変フレームレート（VFR）は使用しないでください' (use MP4; do not include Edit List edit information; make video and audio the same length; include exactly one video and one audio track; do not use variable frame rate). TRAP: the same page documents a separate ショート (vertical short) surface with a much tighter cap: 'ファイルサイズ 6GB以下', '解像度 2160x4096以下', 'アスペクト比 縦長または正方形', '動画の長さ 180秒以下' (vertical or square aspect, up to 180 seconds). So an AnimeEffects export for the Short surface must be 180 s or less and vertical or square, while a normal video upload may be 6 hours. The 3 GB to 6 GB change is a Nico-owned announcement: blog.nicovideo.jp/niconews/233213.html, 2024-10-29, '2024年10月29日（火）より、ニコニコ動画に投稿できる動画の容量が、1本あたり3GBから6GBに倍増しました。'. Concurrent uploads are capped at 5 in-progress videos for Premium and for general members at user level 8 or above, and 1 below that.

label: Nico Nico Seiga (illustration post)
containerCodec: png, jpeg, gif. Animated formats are not documented for the illustration corner, so treat animated GIF and APNG as unsupported until Nico says otherwise.
maxSizeNote: 10 MB per illustration, stated directly in Nico Nico's own help answer. This is a hard posting limit ('サイズは10MBまでです'), not a recommendation.
dimensions: No pixel limit is published for 静画 illustrations. A different submission type, ニコニコ漫画 (manga), does publish manuscript sizes: recommended 1920x1080 and minimum 800x450 for the Nico Nico Manga format, and 650 px wide with height up to 1200 px for the scroll format.
note: The answer body is not in the rendered HTML of the help page but is present verbatim in the page JSON payload, read 2026-09-11. Verbatim: '投稿できるイラストはpng,jpeg,gif形式のイラストで、サイズは10MBまでです。' (illustrations that can be posted are png, jpeg and gif format, and the size may be up to 10 MB). Also verbatim from the same answer: title up to 48 characters, description up to 1000 characters, tag up to 20 characters each, category list (創作 / ファンアート / 殿堂入り), and '画像の公開設定 投稿するイラストの公開／非公開を設定することができます。' Page updated 2025-12-24 and published 2015-09-09. This is NOT an obligation to post only drawn art in a technical sense, it is a content rule ('イラストコーナーは自分で『描いた』イラスト専用です'), which matters for an AI or tool-generated export only as a policy matter. SEPARATE LIMITS, do not mix them up: the manga route is a different submission type with its own numbers, 200 manuscript pages per episode for the Nico Nico Manga format and 50 for the scroll format, and a 2012 press report (internet.watch.impress.co.jp) states 10 MB per manuscript file for manga. UNVERIFIED: whether Nico Nico re-encodes or resizes a posted illustration, whether PNG alpha survives, and whether an animated GIF actually animates in the illustration corner. A 2023 Nico Nico gift-illustration contest rule required 'ファイル形式：背景透過のPNG形式（APNG等のアニメーション不可）' (transparent PNG, no animation such as APNG), but that is a contest rule, not the platform spec, so it must not be generalised. The claim that the illustration corner forbids animated GIF appears only in third-party restatements.

label: Douyin (抖音) video post
containerCodec: Common formats accepted, mp4 and webm recommended ('支持常用视频格式，推荐使用 mp4、webm'). The Android share SDK is stricter and requires mp4 with YUV420P or YUVJ420P pixel format only.
maxSizeNote: CONFLICT INSIDE BYTEDANCE'S OWN DOCUMENTATION, carry both numbers. The Douyin upload-video endpoint says the total video size must be within 4 GB ('视频总大小 4GB 以内'). The chunked-upload init endpoint on the same platform says the video file must not exceed 128 MB ('视频文件大小不超过128MB，时长在15分钟以内') while also repeating the 4 GB total. The two endpoints also disagree on when chunking becomes mandatory (over 300 MB versus over 128 MB). I recorded 4 GB from the upload-video page and flag the 128 MB line, which cannot be correct as a total size next to a 4 GB ceiling. No consumer app or web cap is published by ByteDance at all.
dimensions: Short side must be under 2160 px and long side under 4096 px ('视频尺寸需要满足 短边小于2160且长边小于4096'). Recommended resolution 720p (1280x720) or above. No frame rate is published. Recommendation text is internally odd and is quoted as-is: '为了更好的观看体验，推荐上传 16:9，分辨率为 720p（1280x720）及以上的竖版视频。' (for a better viewing experience we recommend uploading 16:9, 720p (1280x720) or above, vertical video).
note: Verbatim, upload-video endpoint: '超过 50MB 的视频建议采用分片上传，可以降低网关超时造成的失败。超过 300MB 的视频必须采用分片上传。视频总大小 4GB 以内。单个分片建议 20MB，最小 5MB。' (videos over 50 MB should use chunked upload; over 300 MB must use chunked upload; total video size within 4 GB; each chunk 20 MB suggested, 5 MB minimum). Verbatim, chunked-upload init endpoint (developer.open-douyin.com, 更新时间 2024-04-09): '超过128MB的视频必须采用分片上传。视频总大小4GB以内。' and separately '视频文件大小不超过128MB，时长在15分钟以内。' (video file no more than 128 MB, duration within 15 minutes). That 2024-dated page is the older of the two documents. DURATION CONFLICT, two official ByteDance paths: the Douyin OpenAPI chunked-upload page says within 15 minutes, while the Android share SDK says '单视频及视频总时长最大值为 60 分钟。' (maximum duration of a single video, and of the total, is 60 minutes) and '要求 mp4 文件，目前仅支持YUV420P/YUVJ420P格式。'. I recorded 3600 s from the SDK because that is the path a desktop-created file would take when handed to the Douyin app, and flagged the 900 s API figure. The same SDK page documents photo posting: '抖音应用 12.3.0 及以上版本分享多图数量不能超过 35 个' and a required aspect ratio between 1/3 and 3 for image posts. TRAP AND UNVERIFIED FIGURE: the 500 MB app upload cap that circulates in Chinese SEO articles (for example geo.newrank.cn/news/7813, 2026-02-12) is attributed to '《创作者服务协议》第4.2条' and to a 2024 help centre statement. I could not fetch any ByteDance page containing that clause, and the publicly reachable 抖音用户服务协议 (douyin.com/agreements/?id=6773906068725565448) does not render without JavaScript and contains no file size clause in the text I could obtain. So 500 MB is UNVERIFIED and must not be encoded as a Douyin limit. Automated publishing also requires an approved 代替用户发布内容到抖音 capability, and ByteDance warns that videos carrying a third-party brand logo or watermark risk reduced recommendation, takedown or account ban.

label: Facebook (feed video post)
containerCodec: Recommended: H.264 video with AAC audio in an MP4 or MOV file. Accepted upload formats are much wider: 3g2, 3gp, 3gpp, asf, avi, dat, divx, dv, f4v, flv, gif, m2ts, m4v, mkv, mod, mov, mp4, mpe, mpeg, mpeg4, mpg, mts, nsv, ogm, ogv, qt, tod, ts, vob, wmv.
maxSizeNote: No byte cap is published by Meta for an organic Facebook video upload. The 4 GB figure that essentially every guide repeats is Meta's ADVERTISING spec ('Maximum file size: 4 GB' in the Facebook Reels ads guide, and the 4 GB / 240 minute row in the Facebook Video Requirements one-sheeter, which is an ads creative chart listing supported ad objectives), not an organic upload limit. Do not encode 4 GB as a Facebook video cap.
dimensions: Meta's recommended export settings: maximum width 4000 px with dimensions divisible by 16, standard aspect ratios (16:9, 9:16, 1:1), frame rate 30 fps or lower, stereo audio at 44,100 Hz. Maximum width is a recommendation for the editing-software export path, not a hard rejection threshold published anywhere.
note: The feed video surface no longer exists as a separate thing, and that is the most consequential fact in this row. Verbatim from Meta's help page: 'Update (September 2025): All videos on Facebook are now reels. Any video that you post to Facebook will be shared as a reel, regardless of length or orientation. The same export settings and behaviours apply to all video content that you upload. This unifies the video experience for creators and viewers.' Recommended export settings verbatim: 'Format: H.264 video codec with AAC audio, in either MP4 or MOV file format.' 'Resolution and aspect ratio: Maximum width of 4,000 pixels, with dimensions divisible by 16.' 'Frame rate: 30 frames per second (fps) or lower.' 'Audio: Stereo, 44,100 Hz sample rate.' 'File requirements: Avoid edit lists or special boxes in the file container for best compatibility.' Accepted formats verbatim from facebook.com/help/218673814818907: 'We recommend using the MP4 or MOV format, but here's a complete list of the video formats that can be uploaded to Facebook' followed by 3g2 through wmv. STALE NUMBERS THAT MUST NOT BE USED: the Graph API /event/videos endpoint used to document 'If you upload a video with a multi-part HTTP request or by providing a URL to a video, the video cannot exceed 1 GB in size and 20 minutes in duration.' and 'Resumable video uploads can be up to 1.75GB and 45 minutes in duration.' That endpoint now carries 'This edge has been deprecated and can no longer be used.', so 1 GB / 20 min and 1.75 GB / 45 min are dead figures for a current integration. The Graph API Video API publishing path is the live one and documents no size or duration ceiling at all, only a resumable upload flow. HONEST GAP: organic byte cap and organic duration cap are both null because Meta publishes neither. Third-party pages that assert a hard organic 10 GB figure are not backed by any Meta page I could read.

label: Facebook Reels (video post)
containerCodec: .mp4 recommended. Video codecs: H.264 and H.265 recommended, VP9 and AV1 also supported. Video settings from the Reels Publishing API: chroma subsampling 4:2:0, closed GOP 2 to 5 seconds, fixed frame rate, progressive scan. Audio: AAC Low Complexity, stereo, 128 kbps or more, 48 kHz.
maxSizeNote: No organic byte cap is published by Meta. The 4 GB figure is the ADVERTISING figure ('Maximum file size: 4 GB' in Meta's Facebook Reels ads guide) and the Reels Publishing API documents no file size parameter at all. Recorded as null rather than borrowing the ad number.
dimensions: Meta Business Help: recommended format .mp4, recommended resolution 1080p, recommended frame rate 24 to 60 FPS, closed GOP 2 s to 5 s recommended, chroma subsampling 4:2:0, progressive scan. The Reels Publishing API additionally specifies aspect ratio 9 x 16 and resolution 1080x1920 recommended with a minimum of 540x960, and rejects other aspect ratios with error 1363040 ('Aspect ratios for videos need to be between 16x9 and 9x16').
note: TWO META SOURCES DISAGREE ON DURATION, both are carried here. (1) Meta Business Help, Requirements for Facebook Reels: 'In June 2025, the Videos tab on Facebook was renamed to the Reels tab. All videos posted to Facebook are now shared as reels to simplify the way creators produce and share video content on the platform. Reels can be any length or orientation.' (2) The Reels Publishing API (developers.facebook.com/docs/video-api/guides/reels-publishing) still documents: 'Duration | 3 to 90 seconds. A reel published as a story on a Facebook Page can not exceed 60 seconds.', 'Resolution | 1080 x 1920 pixels (recommended). Minimum is 540 x 960 pixels', 'Frame Rate | 24 to 60 frames per second', 'Aspect Ratio | 9 x 16', and its error table: '1363128 ... Reels duration must be between 3 and 90 seconds.' and '1363129 ... Reels frame rate must be between 24 and 60 frames per second'. I recorded 90 s because it is the enforced number on the API path and the conservative value, but the consumer surface no longer enforces a maximum, so a UI that says 'Facebook Reels: 90 seconds maximum' is describing the API, not the app. Codec support is stated twice by Meta: 'Recommended video codec: H.264, H.265' and 'Supported video codec: H.264, H.265, VP9, AV1'. Recommended video support includes HDR. The API path also requires a publicly fetchable file or a local upload to rupload.facebook.com and rejects files hosted on Meta CDN.

label: Facebook (photo post)
containerCodec: Facebook Help Centre recommends JPEG, BMP, PNG, GIF or TIFF. The Graph API photo path takes JPEG and PNG and states that animated photos are not supported.
maxSizeNote: TWO OFFICIAL NUMBERS, and neither is a clean consumer hard cap. Graph API photo reference: 'Animated photos are not supported, and a photo must be less than 10MB in size.' That is the only hard number stated by either source. Facebook Help Centre: 'We recommend uploading photos below 15 MB.' which is a recommendation with no documented rejection, and additionally 'If you're uploading a PNG file, it's best to keep the file size below 1 MB. PNG files larger than 1 MB may appear pixelated.' I recorded 10 MB because it is the only enforced limit, and flagged 15 MB as the softer consumer guidance.
dimensions: No pixel cap is published for photo posts. Facebook stores several renditions per photo (the Graph API photo node exposes an images list), so the largest rendition served is not the uploaded original. PNG files larger than 1 MB are warned to appear pixelated, which is a quality statement rather than a dimension cap.
note: Verbatim, Graph API photo node: 'Animated photos are not supported, and a photo must be less than 10MB in size.' The same sentence appears on the Album Photos reference (developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/reference/album/photos/), so 10 MB is consistent across the API surface. Verbatim, Facebook Help Centre (facebook.com/help/121317464722113 and facebook.com/help/167931376599294, same text on both): 'We recommend uploading JPEG, BMP, PNG, GIF or TIFF files. If you're uploading a PNG file, it's best to keep the file size below 1 MB. PNG files larger than 1 MB may appear pixelated.' and 'Check the size of the photo. We recommend uploading photos below 15 MB.' CONFLICT TO FLAG: the help centre lists GIF among recommended photo formats while the API says animated photos are not supported, so animated content on the photo path is effectively undocumented and may be flattened, converted, or rejected depending on the route. For an animated cutout export, the Facebook video path (which since September 2025 publishes everything as a reel) is the documented route; do not promise an animated photo post. Alpha is recorded as unknown: PNG is accepted and recommended for logo or text graphics, but no Meta page states whether transparency survives the recompression into renditions, and Facebook's own advice for PNGs above 1 MB suggests aggressive re-processing.

label: Tumblr (video post)
containerCodec: MOV or MP4 only. Tumblr transcodes everything toward 720p H.264 MP4.
maxSizeNote: 500 MB per video, hard. Also 20 videos per day and 60 minutes of video per day. Tumblr Premium doubles the daily published-posts and photo/video/audio upload allowances, to 40 video uploads per day.
dimensions: No pixel limit. Tumblr states its own target and asks you to match it: a 720p H.264 MP4, and it recommends HandBrake's General / Creator 720p60 preset with no modifications. So a larger export is accepted but is not what the platform serves.
note: Verbatim from Tumblr's help centre: 'It'll need to be a MOV or MP4 file.' 'You can post up to 20 videos per day.' 'A single video can be up to 10 minutes in length.' 'The video upload size limit is 500 MB per video.' 'The total video time limit per day is 60 minutes.' Re-encode is stated plainly: 'Tumblr will transcode and re-compress all uploaded videos, so some light pixelation and other artifacts may occur. If you encounter that, try exporting the video as close to our transcoder's goal as possible, which is a 720p H.264 MP4.' Also documented: only one video may be uploaded per post, videos cannot be uploaded into a reblog, and a post can hold at most 10 video blocks. FRESHNESS WARNING, be explicit about it in any UI: the help article body carries no update date and its page metadata reads 2016-10-27, so the numbers are old text. They are corroborated by Tumblr's own staff announcement of 2021-06-11 (staff.tumblr.com/post/653731604461682688), which lists 'Videos posted per day: 10 -> 20', 'Video upload size limit: 100MB -> 500MB', 'Single Video time limit: 5 minutes -> 10 minutes', 'Total Video time limit per day: 5 minutes -> 60 minutes', and by changes.tumblr.com (2021-06-08) 'We've increased the video upload limit to 500MB (from 100MB) across the web and the latest versions of the Tumblr mobile apps.' I found no Tumblr-owned statement dated 2025 or 2026, so these are current-but-not-recently-reaffirmed. Third-party scheduling tools restate 500 MB and 10 minutes, which matches.

label: Tumblr (photo post)
containerCodec: JPEG, PNG or WEBP for static images, and GIF for animated. CMYK and other non-RGB files are rejected. Every uploaded GIF is converted to GIFV server-side.
maxSizeNote: 20 MB per static image, hard. Animated GIFs are far tighter: a compressed GIF should be no larger than 5 MB, and an uncompressed GIF under 10 MB will be compressed for you, with a stated fallback that a GIF exceeding 5 MB that cannot be served is reduced to its first frame only. So the effective animation cap on Tumblr is about 5 MB, not 20 MB.
dimensions: Recommended 540x810 px so the dashboard does not scale the image down. The click-through larger version is capped at 2048 px wide and 3072 px tall, so larger sources are wasted. GIFs should be no more than 540 px wide. Up to 30 images or GIFs per post on the web and 10 from the apps.
note: Verbatim: 'Make sure the file is no larger than 20 MB and is in either JPEG, PNG, or WEBP format.' 'We don't support CMYK files or other non-RGB image files, so save the image in RGB and try uploading again.' 'We recommend your images be 540 pixels wide by 810 tall. Stay within that limit to avoid your images being scaled down on the dashboard.' 'That larger version can be up to 2048 pixels wide and 3072 pixels tall.' GIF rules verbatim: 'We recommend that your GIFs be no more than 540 pixels wide.' 'Any GIFs under 3 MB don't get compressed at all. However, we do convert all uploaded GIFs to GIFV.' 'If you're uploading a compressed GIF, the file should be no larger than 5 MB.' 'If your GIF is uncompressed and under 10 MB, we'll do our best to compress the file down for you.' 'if we're unable to successfully serve a GIF that exceeds 5 MB, Tumblr will serve only the first frame.' Looping is recorded as yes because GIF and GIFV loop natively and Tumblr's whole GIF pipeline is built on that, but note that Tumblr does not publish a looping statement. Alpha is unknown: PNG and WEBP can carry alpha and only RGB is accepted, yet no Tumblr page states whether transparency is preserved after the GIFV conversion and image processing. FRESHNESS WARNING: this article body carries no update date and its page metadata reads 2016-10-28; no Tumblr-owned revision dated 2025 or 2026 was found. TRAP: WEBP is accepted for static images but is not listed as an animated format, and APNG is not mentioned at all, so do not assume an animated WEBP or APNG post will animate. Blog posts commonly quote 10 MB for Tumblr images, which matches nothing on this page except the uncompressed-GIF ceiling.

label: Pinterest (video Pin)
containerCodec: Web: .MP4, .M4V. Android and iOS: .MP4, .MOV, .M4V. Video encoding H.264 or H.265.
maxSizeNote: No byte cap is published for an organic video Pin. The 2 GB figure that guides and scheduling tools repeat is Pinterest's ADVERTISING spec ('Max file size: Up to 2GB' on the Review ad specs page), not an organic limit. Recorded as null.
dimensions: Recommended for full-bleed video: 9:16 or 1080x1920. Other accepted ratios listed by Pinterest: 1:2, 2:3, 3:4, 4:5, 1:1. No pixel minimum or maximum is published. Respect the safe zones: top 270 px, left 65 px, right 195 px, bottom 790 px.
note: Verbatim from Pinterest's own Pin spec page: 'File type | Web: .MP4, .M4V Android and iOS: .MP4, .MOV, .M4V;', 'Video encoding | H.264 or H.265', 'Video length | Minimum 4 seconds, maximum 5 minutes', 'Aspect ratio | For full-bleed videos (or videos that take up the entire screen), we recommend using a 9:16 ratio or 1080x1920 pixel size. Other options include: 1:2, 2:3, 3:4, 4:5, or 1:1.' MAJOR TRAP, this is the row most likely to be wrong in the wild: hundreds of guides (including a 2026-08-24 SEO article) state that an organic video Pin may run 4 seconds to 15 minutes with a 2 GB maximum and are citing Pinterest's AD spec page, which does say 'Max file size | Up to 2GB' and 'Video length | Minimum 4 seconds, maximum 15 minutes'. Those are creative requirements for ads, not the organic Pin limits, and the organic maximum is 5 minutes. A 10 minute export that a user was told is fine will be rejected by the organic uploader. Re-encode is recorded as unknown because Pinterest does not state on the Pin spec page that it re-encodes video, even though it serves multiple renditions and does document an automatic overlay on image Pins. Also note that Pinterest's organic video Pin spec does not list GIF, so animated content has no documented image route.

label: Pinterest (image Pin)
containerCodec: BMP, .JPEG, .PNG, .TIFF, .WEBP. GIF is NOT in the organic image Pin list, unlike the ad spec which does accept GIF.
maxSizeNote: Web: 20 MB maximum. Android and iOS: '1 GB recommended'. Both lines are verbatim from the same official table, so the mobile row is a recommendation rather than a cap, and 20 MB is the number a desktop or web upload must satisfy. A desktop export should target 20 MB.
dimensions: No pixel maximum is published for image Pins. Recommended vertical format 2:3, for example 1000x1500, or 9:16 at 1080x1920. Respect the safe zones: top 270 px, left 65 px, right 195 px, bottom 790 px. Pinterest automatically applies a faint tint layer over image Pins with white or near-white backgrounds (#000000 at 4 percent in light mode) and over black or near-black backgrounds (#FFFFFF at 10 percent in dark mode), and states this applies to all organic and paid image Pins and not to videos.
note: Verbatim: 'File type | BMP, .JPEG, .PNG, .TIFF, .WEBP', 'Max file size | Web: 20 MB maximum Android and iOS: 1 GB recommended', 'Title character count | 100 characters max', 'Description | Enter up to 800 characters.' The automatic tint layer is documented in the same article: 'Pinterest adds a faint color layer to image Pins in the home feed with white or black backgrounds. This distinguishes the pins from the app background color and helps to highlight links included in the Pin. This feature applies to all organic and paid image Pins and ad types but does not apply to videos.' That is why re-encode is recorded as yes: the platform demonstrably alters the served image. Alpha is unknown, because transparency is not mentioned anywhere on the spec page even though PNG and WEBP are accepted. Important for an animation tool: an animated GIF has no documented organic Pin route, so if the artwork must animate on Pinterest it has to go out as a video Pin.

label: Snapchat (Spotlight video)
containerCodec: Not published for organic Spotlight submissions. The only format statement Snapchat publishes is for Ads Manager creatives (.mp4 or .mov with H.264), which is a different surface.
maxSizeNote: No byte cap is published for an organic Spotlight submission. The frequently cited 1 GB video limit and 5 MB image limit come from Snapchat's ADVERTISING specifications (businesshelp.snapchat.com, 'File Size | Video: 1 GB or less, Image: 5 MB'), which govern Ads Manager creatives rather than a post made by a person from the app. Recorded as null.
dimensions: Vertical only, and the minimum length is documented: a Spot must be 5 seconds or longer. Still images are explicitly excluded from Spotlight. No maximum duration and no pixel figure are published for organic posts; the 1080x1920 canvas, 9:16 ratio and 3 seconds to 30 minutes range all belong to the Ads Manager spec.
note: Minimum duration and eligibility, verbatim: 'Create a video Snap that's 5 seconds or longer' and 'The Post button appears on the Main Camera preview when you're 16 or older, you're in a region where Spotlight posting is enabled, and your video is 5 seconds or longer.' Vertical requirement, verbatim from creatorhelp.snapchat.com/s/article/creator-content-best-practices: 'Post Vertical Video: Snaps should be vertical videos with sound. Still-image photos, horizontal Snaps, blurry Snaps, and text-only Snaps won't show up in Spotlight.' Two further documented paths into Spotlight: the Send To screen, and 'You can also post to Spotlight by tapping Post to Spotlight from My Account and uploading content as a new Spotlight post'. Content eligibility is governed by snap.com/content-recommendation-guidelines and the Spotlight Guidelines page (help.snapchat.com/hc/en-us/articles/7012287256596), which is a conduct and eligibility document: 'In order to be eligible for algorithmic recommendation beyond the creator's friends or subscribers, Content must meet the standards described in the Content Guidelines for Recommendation Eligibility.' It publishes no size, duration, resolution or codec figures. AD SPEC TRAP: the Ads Manager table gives '3 seconds to 30 minutes (if file size does not exceed 1 GB)', 'Full Screen Canvas | 1080 x 1920px 9:16 aspect ratio', '.mp4 or .mov and H.264 encoded', 'Image: 5 MB', and 'If the video is less than 3 seconds, the video will be looped to meet the 3 second minimum.' None of that is an organic Spotlight limit, so a preset must not promise 30 minutes or 1 GB. UNVERIFIED: the 32 MB and 60 second figures that appear on third-party size guides; nothing at Snap states either. No Snap-owned page dated 2025 or 2026 with organic Spotlight technical specs was found.

label: Dailymotion (video upload)
containerCodec: .MOV, .MPEG4, .MP4, .AVI, .WMV, .MKV, .FLV. Video codecs: H.264/AVC (recommended), H.265/HEVC, DivX, WMV9, MPEG-2. Audio codecs: AAC (recommended), MP3, WMA9, MPEG Layer 2.
maxSizeNote: 4 GB per file for Users, Standard Creators, Pro Trial, Pro Starter and Pro Advanced; 64 GB for Premium Creators and Pro Enterprise. Hard: the help centre states that reaching one of the limits can suspend upload privileges for 24 hours and show an error in the upload interface. The same tier also allows only 15 videos and 10 hours of content per 24 hours.
dimensions: Up to 3840x2160 horizontal or 2160x3840 vertical. Frame rates accepted: 24, 25, 30, 50, 60 FPS. Suggested bitrates: 2 Mbps SD, 6 to 8 Mbps HD, 20 Mbps 4K. Aspect ratio 16:9 recommended for horizontal and 9:16 for vertical; 4:3 creates black bars on the sides. Progressive scan recommended, interlaced accepted.
note: Read 2026-09-11; the page footer states 'Updated 5 hours ago', making this the freshest primary source in this batch. Verbatim: 'Video size | 4 GB per file maximum | 64 GB', 'Content duration | 2 hours per file maximum | Unlimited', 'Upload Volume | 15 videos uploaded per 24 hours | 96 videos uploaded per 24 hours (default)', 'Total Duration | 10 hours of content uploaded per 24 hours | Unlimited', 'Content type | Video content only (no MP3, AAC...) | Video & Audio content', and 'If you reach one of these limits, your upload privileges may be suspended for 24 hours and an error message will be displayed on your upload interface.' The API documentation repeats the same tiering (developers.dailymotion.com/reference/rate-limiting: 'Per video | 2 hours duration and 4 Gb | Unlimited duration, but 64 Gb max'). Because both a byte cap and a duration cap apply, the binding limit for a high-bitrate 4K export is 4 GB, and for a long low-bitrate export it is 2 hours. The unsupported-format error text in Dailymotion's own studio help confirms the accepted container list ('Please reupload your video in one of our supported formats: MOV, MPEG4, MP4, AVI, WMV, MKV, FLV'). Alpha is not supported: no Dailymotion page offers a transparent video path, and the container and codec list contains no alpha-capable combination.

label: Vimeo (video upload)
containerCodec: MP4 and MOV are preferred, but Vimeo accepts a variety of video file types ('Vimeo accepts a variety of video file types, though common formats such as MP4 and MOV are preferred'). Recommended codecs: H.264, Apple ProRes 422 (HQ) or H.265 (HEVC), with AAC-LC audio. Explicitly unsupported: documents (.pdf, .txt, .doc, .docx, .xlsx, .xml), audio files (.mp3, .wav), project files (.prproj, .wlmp, .imovieproj, .camproj), PowerPoint and Keynote files, DVD image files and meeting recordings.
maxSizeNote: SOFT, not a hard cap: 'It is advisable to keep files under 200 GB for a successful upload.' Vimeo's own troubleshooting article treats 200 GB as the cause of the generic failure ('The most common reason for this error is the source file size being above 200 GB or the video length is longer than 24 hours'). Plan allowances sit underneath that and are the real limit for a normal creator: the Starter plan for accounts that joined before 2024-06-17 is documented as 'capped at 60 videos with a maximum file size of up to 250 GB per video', while the free tier is documented by Vimeo as having no per-file limit but only two videos per month and 25 in total, and legacy Basic/Plus/Pro weekly quotas of 500 MB, 5 GB and 20 GB per week. These statements are all Vimeo's own and do not agree, so 200 GB is recorded as an advisory technical ceiling, not a guarantee.
dimensions: No pixel cap published. Vimeo normalises the source: 'All videos uploaded to Vimeo will be converted to square pixels.' and 'Vimeo converts all videos to a constant frame rate and square pixels.' Recommended source settings: constant frame rate at the native rate, pixel aspect ratio 1:1, progressive scan, BT.709 or BT.2020, bit depth 10 or greater, AAC-LC audio at 48 kHz.
note: Verbatim: 'It is advisable to keep files under 200 GB for a successful upload. We also do not support uploads of videos longer than 24 hours.' The 24 hour figure is a hard refusal ('we do not support'), the 200 GB figure is advice that also matches the documented failure mode. ALPHA IS EXPLICITLY UNSUPPORTED, verbatim from help.vimeo.com/hc/en-us/articles/12426489965585: 'Vimeo does not include alpha channel support at this time.' (that article is about iframe transparency and draws the distinction deliberately: 'The transparency discussed here is referring specifically to the iframe (the containing web element), not transparency in any videos you upload.'). So a transparent cutout export must not be pointed at Vimeo; the table's transparent-video destinations (VP9 WebM for OBS and Safari) are the right rows for that. Re-encode is documented indirectly and clearly: files above the ceiling fail with 'The application has received an invalid parameter.' and Vimeo converts frame rate and pixel aspect ratio, which it can only do by re-encoding. The plan-quota figures come from Vimeo's own pages (help.vimeo.com/hc/en-us/articles/12425432485521 for Starter, vimeo.com/video-uploader for the free tier and the legacy weekly quotas), and they conflict with the 200 GB advice, which is why the byte value here is marked soft.

label: DeviantArt (image or animated GIF submission)
containerCodec: Images: JPEG, PNG, GIF. Animations as SWF and FLA. WebP and APNG are not in DeviantArt's documented image list, so an APNG export has no documented route.
maxSizeNote: OFFICIAL CONFLICT, 80 MB versus 95 MB. 'What file types can I submit to DeviantArt?' states 'Images: 80MB'. 'What are the restrictions around what I can submit to DeviantArt?' states '95 MB: Image-based submissions.' Both are DeviantArt help centre articles. I recorded 80 MB because it is the lower of the two, so a file that satisfies it satisfies both. The 30 MB figure quoted in older DeviantArt forum answers (FAQ #753) is obsolete and must not be used.
dimensions: No pixel cap is published. GIF thumbnails are generated automatically from the first frame and 'will display as either moving or static depending on file size, device, and image placement', so the first frame must work as a standalone still. Animated preview images, where a submission still needs one, 'should be 150px or smaller'.
note: Verbatim from the file types article: 'Images: JPEG, PNG, GIF', 'Compressed files: RAR, ZIP, 7-ZIP, DMG, ICONPACKAGER', 'Animations: SWF, FLA', 'File Size Limitations ... Images: 80MB', 'Non-Images: 200MB (1GB for Core Members)'. Verbatim from the restrictions article: '95 MB: Image-based submissions.', '1 GB: Non-image based submissions (such as zipped, or other compressed archives).' The GIF handling rule verbatim: 'GIF file thumbnails are automatically generated, use the first frame as the preview image, and will display as either moving or static depending on file size, device, and image placement. Static previews will be marked with GIF for clarity.' This is the most generous still-animation destination in the whole batch: an animated GIF counts as an image and therefore gets the 80 MB image cap, against 5 MB on Tumblr and 10 MB on Nico Nico Seiga. Looping is recorded as unknown rather than yes because DeviantArt never states that animation loops on the work page, only that a GIF may display as moving or static. Alpha is unknown: PNG is accepted and DeviantArt historically shows PNG transparency, but no help article states whether transparency survives processing. Neither article displays a publication or update date, so freshness cannot be established from the page itself; both are live on the current help domain, and the older help.deviantart.com URLs still serve the same video text. Video submissions are a separate, paid Core Member feature and are recorded in their own row.

label: DeviantArt (video or film submission, Core Members)
containerCodec: AVI, MPEG, MPG, MPE, MP4, MKV, WebM, MOV, OGV, VOB, M4V, 3GP, DivX, XVID, MXF, WMV, M1V, FLV, M2TS.
maxSizeNote: 1 GB, and video submission is a paid Core Member feature, so this destination is not available to a free account at all. Minimum duration 10 seconds. Duration ceiling depends on the membership tier, which is why the byte cap and the duration cap must be read together.
dimensions: Recommended resolution 1920x1080. The first frame of the video is used as the file preview image, so the first frame must stand alone. No pixel maximum is published.
note: Verbatim: 'Video submissions are a Core Member feature.', 'Video (for Core Members only): 1GB', 'Video files must be at least 10 seconds.', 'For Core and Core+ Members, videos can be up to 12 minutes in length. For Core Pro and Pro+, there is no limit to video length.', 'The recommended resolution is 1920 x 1080. The first frame of the video will be used as the file's preview image.' The same 10 second to 12 minute and under 1 GB text appears on DeviantArt's older help page help.deviantart.com/856 ('Core Members can submit video files that are between 10 seconds and 12 minutes long and smaller than 1GB in size.'), so the tiers are consistent across both help surfaces. I recorded 720 s because it is the ceiling for the base Core and Core+ tiers; a Core Pro or Pro+ account has no documented length limit, so the UI must not present 12 minutes as a universal rule. The video byte cap is 1 GB on every tier, so a 12 minute export needs to fit in 1 GB, which is roughly 11 Mbps. Alpha is recorded as no: an alpha-capable master would have to be VP9 WebM or ProRes 4444, and DeviantArt documents no alpha or transparency support for video.

label: Newgrounds (animation or movie upload)
containerCodec: SWF plus most video formats, with MP4, MOV and WMV named by name. Newgrounds' own converter tooling exports H.264 in an MP4 container by default, so H.264 MP4 is the practical target.
maxSizeNote: HONEST GAP, no byte cap is published by Newgrounds anywhere I could read. The wiki states only that a limit exists on the upload form and that it can be raised on request. A forum post states 100 MB for SWF and 6.3 GB for video (newgrounds.com/bbs/topic/1444458), but a member forum post is not a primary source, so no number is recorded here.
dimensions: Supported resolutions published by Newgrounds: 3840x2160 (4K), 1920x1080, 1280x720, 640x380. 16:9 is called the standard aspect ratio. Suggested bitrates: 40 to 50 Mbps for 3840x2160, 10 to 20 Mbps for 1920x1080, 5 to 10 Mbps for 1280x720. Thumbnails are expected to be at least 480x270 for games and movies.
note: Verbatim: 'Newgrounds accepts video in most common formats (MP4, MOV, WMV) as well as SWF.' and 'Newgrounds accepts movies in SWF and most video formats (MP4, MOV, etc). They can all be uploaded via the same form.' The no-published-cap finding is itself quoted: 'It is best to upload the highest quality version you can within our upload limits specified on the upload form.' and from the content submission wiki, 'If your filesize limit is too small, you may request a raise.' plus 'You may submit a maximum of two per day.' So the limit is per-account, displayed only on the signed-in upload form, and negotiable, which means a preset must not invent one. Re-encode is recorded as no-partial because Newgrounds documents exactly that behaviour for audio: 'If you upload with an AAC bitrate of 192 kbps or less it will not be re-encoded on our end for 2160p and 1080p formats. For 720p and 360p, we will re-encode the audio to 128k and 96k respectively. This is why it's best to upload the highest quality audio you can, preferably one of the lossless formats mentioned above.' Video is served at the uploaded rendition ladder, and the audio note implies 720p and 360p renditions exist. Looping is a first-class documented upload option, verbatim from the project system announcement: 'Examples include setting an MP4 file to loop'. Alpha is unknown: SWF is accepted and can carry transparency, but no Newgrounds page states an alpha video path, and H.264 in MP4 cannot carry alpha. The Art Portal is a separate, still-image surface and is not covered by this row.

label: pixiv (illustration post)
containerCodec: JPG (.jpg or .jpeg), PNG, GIF. Explicitly not supported: bitmap, animated GIF and animated PNG. If several images in different formats are posted together, all of them are converted to JPG.
maxSizeNote: 32 MB per image and 200 MB per post, both stated by pixiv's own help centre. pixiv's own announcement of 2018-07-17 raised these from 8 MB per illustration and 30 MB per upload batch. WARNING: the 8 MB figure is still repeated by many blogs and by at least one 2026 article that instead claims 10 MB, and neither matches the current pixiv number.
dimensions: No pixel limit is published by pixiv. A third-party claim of a 32768 px per-side maximum could not be confirmed on any pixiv page. One documented consequence matters for cutout artwork: posting multiple files in mixed formats converts every file to JPG, which flattens any alpha, so a transparent PNG should be posted on its own.
note: Verbatim, English help centre: 'Illustrations are limited to 32 MB per image. The entire post is limited to 200 MB.' and from the posting guide, 'Each file must be no more than 32MB. You can post JPG, GIF, or PNG files. You cannot post animated GIFs.' Format rules verbatim, Japanese help centre: 'pixivではJPG、GIF、PNGでの投稿ができます。それぞれ拡張子は .jpg(.jpeg) .gif .png です。ビットマップ(.bmp)、アニメーションGIF、アニメーションPNGは投稿できません。' (pixiv accepts JPG, GIF and PNG with those extensions; bitmap, animated GIF and animated PNG cannot be posted) and '複数の画像を異なる拡張子でまとめて投稿された場合、全てJPGに変換されます。' (if multiple images with different extensions are posted together, all are converted to JPG). The 32 MB and 200 MB figures are pixiv's own change announcement: pixiv.net/info.php?id=4688, 2018-07-17, 'Single illustration size Before: up to 8MB -> After: up to 32MB' and 'Uploaded files at once Before: up to 30MB -> After: up to 200MB'. FRESHNESS: the 2018 announcement is older than 2025, but the limits are restated on current pixiv help pages with no newer revision found, so 32 MB and 200 MB are treated as current. Alpha is unknown: a single transparent PNG is accepted and pixiv does not state that it flattens it, but the documented mixed-format conversion to JPG proves there is at least one path that destroys alpha. Loops are no because animated GIF and APNG are both explicitly rejected. Animated art belongs in pixiv's ugoira format, which is already covered by its own row in the existing research file, and ugoira has different numbers (150 PNG or JPEG frames, 8 MB per frame, 30 MB total, or a single animated GIF of 16 MB up to 500 frames).

label: Instagram (feed photo post)
containerCodec: JPEG only. Instagram's content publishing documentation states 'JPEG is the only image format supported. Extended JPEG formats such as MPO and JPS are not supported.' PNG and WebP are not accepted by the publishing API.
maxSizeNote: 8 MB maximum, hard, from the official image specification. Instagram's consumer help centre publishes no byte figure for a feed photo, so 8 MB is the documented container limit and the number an export must satisfy.
dimensions: Aspect ratio must be within a 4:5 to 1.91:1 range. Minimum width 320 px, scaled up if smaller. Maximum width 1440 px, scaled down if larger. Height varies with width and aspect ratio. Colour space sRGB, and images using other colour spaces have them converted to sRGB.
note: Verbatim from the IG User Media reference, page footer 'Updated: Aug 12, 2026', read 2026-09-11: 'Format: JPEG', 'File size: 8 MB maximum.', 'Aspect ratio: Must be within a 4:5 to 1.91:1 range', 'Minimum width: 320 (will be scaled up to the minimum if necessary)', 'Maximum width: 1440 (will be scaled down to the maximum if necessary)', 'Color Space: sRGB. Images using other color spaces will have their color spaces converted to sRGB.' Extra documented mechanics that matter for an exporter: publishing is a two step container flow and the container must be published within 24 hours or it expires ('Containers expire after 24 hours'), an account may create only 400 containers per rolling 24 hours, and the image must be reachable at a public URL for Meta to fetch. Alpha cannot survive because JPEG has no alpha channel, so a transparent cutout export cannot be delivered as an Instagram feed photo; the same page documents Reels separately (300 MB, 15 minutes maximum, 3 seconds minimum, 1920 px maximum horizontal, HEVC or H.264), which is already covered by the existing research file. Note also that this is the professional/business account API path; Instagram's in-app uploader is not documented at this level of detail anywhere Meta publishes, so the byte and width numbers should be presented as the API specification.
